newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan sees fiscal improvement this year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan sees fiscal improvement this year.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the public sector deficit would improve this year and in 1997.
"There will be a clear improvement in the fiscal situation in 1996, compared with 1995, and in 1997 we will have an improvement compared with 1996," Malan said.

He said the government had to consider "four dimensions" when addressing the fiscal situation, including the federal administration, public sector companies, the welfare system and states and municipalities.

"The way forward for public sector companies is privatization," he said. "Over time, public sector companies' contribution to the fiscal deficit will decline in line with the progress of privatization."

Malan said states and municipalities would also help improve the fiscal situation. He said the federal government had already signed agreements with 19 state governors in which the states committed themselves to making fiscal adjustments between 1996 and 1998.
Malan said welfare reform would be back on the agenda in Congress after October's municipal elections.

"We are convinced that the welfare system will have to be changed, if not this year, then next year or in three, four, five years time," Malan said. "The present system is unsustainable and profoundly unjust."
He said improvements on the federal administration side depended to a large extent on the advances made in the other three areas.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
